title: A Lean formalization of dual-sourcing submodularity and optimal-order existence
description:
Two complete Lean proofs for the actual two-supplier random-capacity expected-profit model: lattice submodularity in feasible orders, and existence of a global maximizing nonnegative order with each coordinate zero, equal to design capacity, or having an existing zero partial derivative. Both complete Prove2Me target signatures are proved. Demand is nonnegative with finite mean; the second theorem additionally assumes absolute continuity. Positive capacities, nonnegative revenue, penalty and costs, committed-cost fractions in [0,1], and v<r+p are explicit model hypotheses. The disclosed platform qualifications are retained.

The submodularity proof establishes all required profit integrabilities before integrating a pointwise lattice inequality. The existence proof combines a uniform profit Lipschitz bound, clipping to a compact capacity box, null kink events under the atomless-capacity and absolutely-continuous-demand laws, differentiation under the integral and Fermat's condition. It proves no sufficient first-order condition, explicit CDF derivative formula, region-by-region optimizer or comparative statics. No downstream automatic closure is claimed.

The original model and results are due to Yimin Wang, Wendell Gilland and Brian Tomlin, Mitigating Supply Risk: Dual Sourcing or Process Improvement?, Manufacturing & Service Operations Management 12(3), 489–510 (2010), DOI 10.1287/msom.1090.0279, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 on p. 494. The author-hosted published PDF was inspected and hashed; the online proof appendix was not inspected. This packet supplies its own checked argument and cites, rather than redistributes, the paper. mikedeng1 supplied the platform formulation and disclosed qualifications; Shuze Chen reviewed the platform statements, not these proofs. Theorem 1 reuses the accepted queelius Lemma 1 source inline, with the top-level declaration renamed. That reuse is not another counted result.

The self-contained packet includes unchanged accepted sources, independent full-type and axiom audits with autoImplicit=false, the sole required platform definition, immutable Lean 4.33.1 and Mathlib pins, the established archive verifier, fresh reproduction logs and three rejected controls: changed proof bytes, a weakened target and an added local axiom. Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are proof axioms. Verified third-party compiled caches remain trusted inputs.

Alexander Richard Towell directed the research and publication; OpenAI Codex substantially developed, checked, submitted and documented the formalizations. Lean and Mathlib contributors retain foundational credit. Mathematical novelty, exhaustive priority assessment, source-author endorsement and independent human proof review are not claimed. Original platform submissions and acceptances occurred on October 21, 2026. This first coherent archive is a separate publication event and adds no new accepted target.
notes: Two accepted complete formalizations of established source results. Original mathematical and platform contributors are predecessors, not represented as coauthors. A DOI provides an archival citation, not proof of novelty or peer review.
